Thanks for flagging those, Carlos — adding a few technical items we should cover and a short pre-call checklist so the core session can focus on architecture and trade-offs. Attaching a quick snapshot (redwood-arch-snapshot.png) that we'll walk through.

Parking-lot (proposed additions):
  • VPN & egress constraints (Carlos' doc attached) — need to confirm NAT ranges, egress filtering, and whether outbound TLS inspection is applied.
  • Sizing: clarify burst vs sustained QPS, average concurrency, and SLAs for tail latency.
  • Model characteristics: typical sequence length, prompt templates, embedding vs generation mix, and whether you plan to use system messages or long-context sessions.
  • KV cache expectations — do you anticipate heavy prefix reuse (caching benefits) or mostly one-offs?
  • Data residency / private deployment requirements (if you need an on-prem or VPC deployment).
  • Acceptable quantization/profile choices — e.g., fp16 vs 8-bit QAT/ptq if model owners require bit-level audits.

Quick checklist for your team (so we can prepare demo assets):
  1) Sample payloads (anonymized) or size-distribution for tokens per request.
  2) Expected peak and 95/99th latency targets.
  3) Any proxy/load-balancer timeouts (idle and active).
  4) Contact for infra-level questions (Emma's role looks like the right person).

If you can drop the sample payload & peak numbers before the session we can produce a rapid sizing estimate and a few config suggestions to discuss. Happy to do a 20m sync with Emma and one of our infra engineers if that helps.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
